scope: SeatMap_TestCases.csv (NDC_Integration/TestCases/SeatMap_TestCases.csv) - targeted run of 11 test cases: TC-SEATMAP-POS-02, VAL-03, VAL-04, VAL-07, VAL-08, VAL-09, VAL-10, BIZ-03, BIZ-04, SEC-01, SEC-02 - user-requested Round 12

text: Targeted, user-requested run of 11 SeatMap test cases (not the full SeatMap_TestCases.csv suite). The disk log was written in one batch after execution rather than per test case in real time, so each test case's reporting_started_at/reporting_ended_at brackets a real full Markdown re-render taken at write-up time, not at verdict time. TC-SEATMAP-VAL-07, VAL-08, VAL-09 and VAL-10 are read off one shared GetSeatMap response (chain A2), so their timing spans are that call's span; the inline analysis time is folded into it. HEADLINE: every Book call on staging failed this round with HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (SocketException 'Name or service not known') after 34-48 seconds, yet the failure envelopes embed a 'Booking Confirmation' e-mail for a REAL ticketed booking, and re-submitting the same offer returns 'This booking has already been created (609)'. This is the Round 8 BUG-16 pattern (booking silently created, no PNR returned), now with a different status code and with the booking identifiers recoverable from the envelope. Because no Book response carried pnr/bookingToken, the Book-response assertions of TC-SEATMAP-POS-02 and TC-SEATMAP-VAL-03 could not be evaluated and are BLOCKED (same convention as Round 8). TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04 and TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-04 could still be judged from the evidence the failure envelopes and later seat maps provide. The x-api-key is never written to the log; raw OriginalSupplierRequest payloads (credentials, e-mail recipient details) are replaced by a redaction marker.

title: Verify GetSeatMap sets getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID and Book consumes them as ResponseId/selectedOfferId when SeatMap precedes it
request_summary: Book (GulfAir/KSA, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01, 1 ADT, no seat) with ResponseId/selectedOfferId taken straight from the GetSeatMap response; tried on 3 independent chains
response_summary: 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 on all 3 attempts (34.0s, 34.2s, 36.9s) - no pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR returned; GetSeatMap itself returned 200 with non-empty offerId/responseId each time
expected: GetSeatMap returns 200 with non-empty offerId/responseId; Book accepts them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without AddPassenger IDs being re-sent
actual: GetSeatMap half confirmed (200, offerId/responseId non-empty and equal to the AddPassenger values). Book half could not be evaluated: Book accepted the IDs (it created real bookings RIPLBZ, TVQBBV, RCEVKA) but answered 409 with no pnr, so the 'returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR' assertion has no response to check. Blocked by BUG-16 (Book silently succeeds while returning an error).
evidence: 3 of 3 Book calls 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 / SocketException; confirmation e-mail inside each envelope shows a real booking: RIPLBZ, TVQBBV (ticket 722136996973), RCEVKA (ticket 722136996974), each 993.00 SAR; GetSeatMap responseId a87b75c4-8562-4de9-88ec-6ac2947e38a0 == AddPassenger responseId a87b75c4-8562-4de9-88ec-6ac2947e38a0

title: Verify cellID round-trips into Book passengersSelectedSeats.setSegmentsSeats.cellId despite casing difference (cellID vs cellId)
request_summary: Book (GulfAir/KSA, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01, 1 ADT) on the chain A2 offer with seat 12C and cellId = the verbatim cellDetails.cellID from that offer's GetSeatMap response
response_summary: 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 'This booking has already been created (609)' in 1.7s - no pnr, no seat echo
expected: Book accepts the token despite the field-name casing difference and attaches the correct seat, echoed in passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats
actual: Not evaluable. The offer used here had already been silently booked by the POS-02 attempt (BUG-16), so Book answered 'booking already created' before looking at the seat, and a Book on a fresh offer would only have returned the same 409-without-pnr envelope, so there is no seat echo to check. No new booking was made for this case, to avoid piling up untracked live bookings. The cellID/cellId casing question stays CONFIRMED from Rounds 1-11 (case-insensitive binding); it was not re-tested.
evidence: Book (seat 12C, verbatim cellID) -> 409 'This booking has already been created (609)' on chain A2's offer; seat 12C on chain A2's GetSeatMap: AvailablePaid 60.00 SAR

title: Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer
endpoint_or_flow: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (x2 offers) -> Book
request_summary: Book using Offer C's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but cellId taken from Offer B's GetSeatMap (seat 12C token), cellCode=12B (valid on Offer C); two fresh Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains
response_summary: 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 after 47.7s (the Book-wide failure, see BUG-16) - not a validation rejection; the envelope's embedded confirmation e-mail shows booking REGOSM, ticket 722136996975, total 1053.00 SAR
expected: Request is rejected with a 4xx validation error (exact shape UNKNOWN per 7.9) because the cellID token embeds the originating ResponseId/OfferId and is bound to the offer it was issued for
actual: STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07, 8th confirmed occurrence). The foreign cellId was not rejected: Book ran the full supplier round-trip and created a real, ticketed booking with seat 12B priced in (total 1053.00 SAR = 993.00 + 60.00). The Book response itself was the Book-wide 409 (BUG-16), so this verdict rests on the booking record embedded in the envelope plus seat 12B disappearing from later seat maps, not on a 200 echo.
evidence: booking REGOSM, ticket 722136996975, fare 640.00 + 353.00 + seat 60.00 = 1053.00; seat 12B: AvailablePaid before, NoSeat on Offer B re-read and on a fresh Offer D afterwards (see TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-04); an earlier, faster 'already created' reject (1.4s) on a previously-used offer is NOT evidence and is ignored

title: Verify window/aisle/extra-legroom/exit-row seat attributes are programmatically derivable from cellCharacteristics for every Seat-category cell
request_summary: One GetSeatMap response (GulfAir/KSA, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01, 1 ADT) - all 176 Seat cells read and classified (Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chain executed first)
response_summary: 200 - 30 rows x 7 columns; 176 Seat cells, 30 Aisle cells, 4 NoSeat cells; 797 cellCharacteristics entries, every padisCode = "Unknown"
expected: For codes in the sourced canonical PADIS table the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text; codes outside the table are logged, not failed
actual: Every Seat cell carries a derivable window/aisle/centre marker in its description text; 0 of 176 contradict their column position (A/F=WINDOW, C/D=AISLE_SEAT, B/E=CENTER_SEAT, left/right side consistent for all 176). Extra-legroom (LEG_SPACE_SEAT rows 8, 19, 20), bulkhead (row 8) and exit-row (EXIT_ROW_SEAT rows 18-21, 24 seats) are derivable from the text too. padisCode is "Unknown" for 797/797 characteristics, so the PADIS-code route yields nothing for this supplier; attributes are derivable only from the description text (logged, not failed, per the expected result). Unchanged from Rounds 1-11.
evidence: column/description mismatches: 0 of 176; WINDOW=59, AISLE_SEAT=59, CENTER_SEAT=58; EXIT_ROW_SEAT=24 (rows 18-21); LEG_SPACE=16 (rows 8,19,20); BULKHEAD=4; padisCode Unknown=797/797

title: Verify overall cellAvailability and per-passenger seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries are independently reported and internally consistent (not required to list every passenger)
request_summary: GetSeatMap for a fresh 3-passenger offer (2 ADT + 1 CHD, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01) - every cell compared against passengersSeatMapAvailability
response_summary: 200 - 176 Seat cells; PAX1/PAX2/PAX3 each have a 176-code allow-list; every cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger lists PAX1, PAX2 and PAX3
expected: A passenger listed in a cell seatPriceDetailsByPassenger should also have that cellCode in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability allow-list; absence is valid, completeness is NOT asserted; overall and per-passenger availability may legitimately differ
actual: Internally consistent: 528 passenger-cell price entries (176 x 3), 0 listed for a cell absent from that passenger's allow-list, 0 allow-list codes without a priced cell. GulfAir lists all three passengers on every cell (so the 'absence is valid' branch could not be exercised - fine, it is not required), and per-passenger paxCellAvailability equals the overall cellAvailability everywhere (0 differences; all AvailablePaid). For context: the CHD passenger is offered every exit-row cell (24/24), the already-tracked BUG-09.
evidence: cells=176; listed-pax-set [PAX1,PAX2,PAX3]=176 cells; listed-but-not-in-allow-list=0; allow-list-but-not-priced=0; paxCellAvailability != cellAvailability: 0; CHD PAX3 present on 24/24 EXIT_ROW_SEAT cells

title: Apply the three universal caller-facing security checks (invalid x-api-key, invalid Client-Id, cross-tenant supplier/credentialsSelector) to GetSeatMap
request_summary: GetSeatMap with a valid KSA-issued offer (chain A2): (1) invalid x-api-key, (2) invalid Client-Id, (3a) supplier/selector switched to TravelportNdc/UAE, (3b) same supplier GulfAir with credentialsSelector switched to UAE; extra probes: empty x-api-key, bogus selector, omitted selector
response_summary: (1) 401 AuthenticationError; (2) 401 AuthenticationError; (3a) 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "Failed to deserialize the selected offer"; (3b) 200 - the full seat map was returned; extras: empty key 401, bogus selector 400, omitted selector 400
expected: All three variants rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN; reuse the envelope other endpoints produce)
actual: Two of the three checks pass cleanly, the third only half-passes. Switching to a different SUPPLIER is rejected (400), but switching only the credentialsSelector to another VALID one for the same supplier (GulfAir/UAE, a real GulfAir tenant) is NOT rejected: GetSeatMap returns the complete seat map for an offer created under KSA. So credentialsSelector is still not enforced as an authorization boundary on GetSeatMap (BUG-17, reproduced for the 2nd time), contradicting SPEC.md 7.14's description of supplier/credentialsSelector as the API's implicit authorization boundary.
evidence: control 200; badKey 401 AuthenticationError "Invalid authorization header"; badClient 401 (same envelope); supplier switch 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 SelectedOfferId "Failed to deserialize the selected offer"; GulfAir/UAE with a KSA offer 200 (~198 KB body, offerId/responseId returned, responseId equal to the KSA offer's)

title: Record that supplier-side authentication security and request/response logging are not independently verifiable through this API black-box contract
request_summary: N/A - documentation/scope-boundary case, no live API call
expected: Documented per 1.5/1.8/PRD 7: AC8 (supplier-side authentication) and the logging half of AC9 are confirmable only via a backend credential/config audit and log/observability review, not through this suite; AC9 graceful-error half is covered by TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05
actual: Documented as specified; SPEC.md 1.5/1.8 and NDC_PRD.md 7 (Gap #1: hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id) re-checked and still say the same. AC8/AC9 must not be marked covered by API tests without the paired backend/config/log audit. Unchanged from Rounds 1-11.
evidence: No API call made, per the test case's own definition; SPEC.md headings 1.5 and 1.8 present (2/2) and the PRD Gap #1 line present (1/1)

expected_value: HTTP 200 with {"pnr":"<real PNR>","bookingToken":"<token>","gdsPNR":"<value or empty>"} - a booking that was created must be reported as created
evidence: 4 of 4 fresh Book calls 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (34.0s, 34.2s, 36.9s, 47.7s) with Context SocketException "Name or service not known"; each envelope's embedded confirmation e-mail shows a real booking: RIPLBZ/722136996972, TVQBBV/722136996973, RCEVKA/722136996974, REGOSM/722136996975 (993.00 SAR; REGOSM 1053.00 SAR incl. seat); re-submits on used offers -> 409 "This booking has already been created (609)".
summary: Book returns HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (SocketException "Name or service not known") after 34-48 seconds while the booking is actually created and ticketed: the envelope embeds the booking's confirmation e-mail, and re-submitting the same offer answers "This booking has already been created (609)". The caller never receives a pnr/bookingToken.
impact: Real ticketed bookings are created with no identifier returned to the caller, so they cannot be tracked, voided or cancelled through the API; every Book-dependent test (POS-02, VAL-03) is blocked. New root-cause clue versus Round 8: the failure appears to be in the post-booking confirmation-e-mail step (DNS failure), not the supplier call. The failure envelopes also expose recipient contact details, PNR and ticket number.
history: First observed Round 8 (2026-09-09, as HTTP 500 + "already created (609)" on retry); not reproduced in Rounds 9, 10, 11 (Book returned a clean 200); reproduced again Round 12 (2026-09-30) on 4 of 4 fresh Book calls, now as HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999.

expected_value: 4xx validation error rejecting a cellId that does not belong to this offer, with no booking created
evidence: Book on Offer C (cellCode 12B) with Offer B's 12C cellId ran the full ~48s booking path and created booking REGOSM / ticket 722136996975, total 1053.00 SAR = 993.00 + 60.00 seat; seat 12B then disappeared from every later seat map.
summary: Book accepts a cellId issued for a different offer's GetSeatMap response and creates a ticketed booking with the seat attached and priced.
impact: The cellId token is not validated at all; seat selection is driven purely by cellCode, so a stale, foreign or forged token still gets a caller charged and ticketed for the seat. This round the evidence comes from the booking record inside the BUG-16 envelope, not from a 200 echo.
history: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed Rounds 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11 and now 12 (Round 4 blocked by an outage; Rounds 8-10 did not exercise it).

expected_value: 4xx rejection (offer not found / not authorized for this credentialsSelector), as happens when the supplier is switched
evidence: Offer created under GulfAir/KSA; GetSeatMap with GulfAir/UAE -> 200, full seat map (~198 KB, same responseId); supplier switched to TravelportNdc/UAE -> 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; invalid key/Client-Id -> 401 AuthenticationError.
summary: GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector).
impact: credentialsSelector is the API's per-tenant boundary (SPEC.md 7.14). A caller holding an offerId/responseId from one tenant (KSA) can read that offer's seat map through another tenant's selector (UAE), so cross-tenant isolation depends solely on offer IDs being unguessable. Other offer-consuming endpoints (Book, GetAncillary, FareCheck) were not tested.
history: First observed Round 11 (2026-09-29); reproduced again Round 12 (2026-09-30).

summary: The "This booking has already been created (609)" 409 envelope again echoes the full upstream SOAP request including live apiKey/secretKey in plaintext (seen on both re-submitted Book calls; values not recorded here).
The CHD passenger (PAX3) is offered every exit-row seat (24 of 24 EXIT_ROW_SEAT cells in its allow-list).

label: Setup before the first test case
steps: Read the Execute_Test_cases skill and its execution-mechanics reference (request templates, ID chaining, report template).
Read the Generate_QA_Report skill, the log schema and the Round 11 Markdown report so this run follows the same conventions.
Read the CSV rows for the 11 requested test cases.
Pulled Round 11's request bodies (Search, AddPassenger for 1 and for 3 passengers) out of its log and saved them as templates.
Wrote the PowerShell helper library (HTTP client, redaction, chain builder), created the run slug and logged run_start.
Hit a PowerShell parameter error in the Book helper, fixed it, and rebuilt the first chain before the first Book call.

label: After the Book failure on chain A2, before the BIZ-03 chain
steps: Read the 409 error body in detail: error code, SocketException context and the embedded email payload - the first sign that a booking had really been created.
Inspected the seat-map cell structure (passengersDetails allow-lists, cellCharacteristics) on chain A2.
Ran the checks for TC-SEATMAP-VAL-07 (window/aisle/exit-row), VAL-08 (pricing), VAL-09 (unique codes) and VAL-10 (rows, zones, columns) on that one seat map.
Decided to run the cases that do not need Book first, while Book was failing.

label: After BIZ-03, before SEC-01
steps: Read the BIZ-03 output: 528 passenger price entries, none outside an allow-list, and the child offered all 24 exit-row seats.
Wrote the SEC-01 script with the 8 request variants (control, wrong key, wrong client, two cross-tenant switches and three extra probes).

label: After SEC-01, before the third Book attempt
steps: Read the SEC-01 results: invalid key/client rejected, supplier switch rejected, GulfAir/UAE on a KSA offer accepted (BUG-17 again).
Decided to re-probe Book on a brand-new offer.
Ran Search, FareConfirm, AddPassenger and GetSeatMap for chain A3 (about 12 seconds); its Book call is the next interval.

label: After the third Book failure, before VAL-03
steps: Confirmed Book was still failing identically (third time) and told the user.
Decided to send one real attempt for each seat-carrying Book shape (VAL-03, VAL-04) and to re-read the seat map afterwards for BIZ-04.
Wrote that script: picked seats 12C and 12B from the seat maps and built the passengersSelectedSeats payloads.

label: After the VAL-03 attempt, before the fresh VAL-04 chains
steps: Read the VAL-03 result: "This booking has already been created (609)" - the reused offer had already been silently booked by an earlier attempt.
Ran the first BIZ-04 seat-map re-reads and a quick VAL-04 try on used offers (fast 409); none of it counted as evidence because the offers were already booked, so those calls are not in the report.
Started two fresh chains (Offer B and Offer C) for a clean VAL-04 run.

label: After BIZ-04, before writing the results to the log
steps: Read the VAL-04 and BIZ-04 results (Book took 47.7 seconds; seat 12B gone from later seat maps).
Decoded the confirmation email inside each 409 error body to recover the PNRs and ticket numbers, and found the seat fare in the Offer C booking (1053 SAR).
Checked SPEC.md and the PRD lines needed for TC-SEATMAP-SEC-02, and read Round 8 and the bug-report template to decide BLOCKED versus FAIL.
Wrote the log-writer script; fixed a syntax error, a wrong ticket-number pattern and a duplicated write before the final run.

label: After the last test-case log write, before the bug reports
steps: Wrote the findings (BUG-16, BUG-07, BUG-17 plus the BUG-11 and BUG-09 re-confirmations), the not-reproduced note and the four cleanup entries to the log.
Closed the Test Execution phase and logged run_end.
Checked the bug-report template and the Round 8 and Round 11 bug reports before drafting.

label: After the bug reports, before the final report generation
steps: Read the HTML report template and the Time Breakdown template.
Wrote the two page generators (Node scripts), ran the first pass to measure render time, and logged the report-generation operations.
